PullRequest.Title: Update VSC model F prompt
PullRequest.Body:

Scenarios.Scenario: A user sends an agent request or continues a tool-calling turn using the vscModelF family.
Scenarios.CriticalPath: AgentPrompt resolves VSCModelPromptF, renders VSC_MODEL_F_SYSTEM_PROMPT into the request messages, serializes the request body, and waits for the model network response. Prompt rendering and the outbound model request are on the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send the rendered agent messages to the model endpoint over HTTP, or through the existing WebSocket request path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One outbound model request per agent round, plus unchanged existing retry behavior; effective multiplicity scales with conversation/tool-call rounds, not with the four removed prompt lines.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same request was sent at the same frequency and concurrency, with four additional fixed system-prompt lines in every vscModelF request body.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The request and streamed response gate progress for each agent round.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize the request JSON containing the rendered system prompt for transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per HTTP model request; the WebSocket path likewise serializes one existing request per round.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The request body contained the same prompt plus four extra fixed lines, so serialization and transmitted bytes were slightly larger before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Serialization occurs before request dispatch, but this diff reduces the fixed message content rather than increasing it.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: The relevant multiplicity is the number of vscModelF model rounds in a conversation. The diff removes a constant amount of text from every round, so CPU, allocation, tokenization, and transmitted-byte costs weakly decrease as rounds increase.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One model request is issued for a given agent round; later tool-call rounds issue additional requests sequentially through the existing loop. HTTP retry or stateful-marker retry behavior is unchanged by this diff, and no new parallelism is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: There is no changed client-side cache or cache key in this hunk. A server-side prompt-prefix cache may be cold when the deployed prompt text changes, as with any prompt update, but subsequent requests share the new shorter stable prefix; no repeated miss, negative-cache behavior, or cache-lifecycle regression is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed constant is directly rendered by VSCModelPromptF on each AgentPrompt render and reaches the existing model request body; the diff only deletes text and adds no work, retained state, or boundary calls.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact token reduction and any provider-side prefix-cache behavior are not measured, but the changed resource direction is clear: fewer fixed characters are rendered and transmitted, with unchanged request count and scheduling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The change slightly reduces per-request serialization, tokenization, and network payload while preserving existing boundary cardinality and concurrency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over the sole changed hunk and traced VSC Model F prompt rendering through model request serialization and HTTP/WebSocket dispatch. The PR removes fixed prompt text, introduces no extra work, fan-out, retention, cache-lifecycle problem, or critical-path boundary, and does not provide evidence of a shipped performance regression fix requiring blame.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
